headline: Committee defers Bill 99 on nepotism, discusses Board of Ethics enforcement time limits

meeting.body: Maui County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
meeting.summary: The committee deferred Bill 99 and discussed Bill 55, which would let the Board of Ethics pursue violations for up to six years. The chair said the bills will return, with no date set yet.
meeting.recap: A testifier who served on the Board of Ethics spoke in favor of Bills 55, 99, and 100.[[0:15:00]] The Board of Ethics chair said the board lost three recent cases because the employees had left county service.[[0:57:24]] Bill 55 would let the Board of Ethics pursue violations for up to six years after a worker leaves county jobs.[[1:12:31]] A proposed new version would start the six-year clock when the violation happened instead.[[1:12:46]] The board's executive director said a full-time investigator will start August 17.[[1:26:31]] A council member moved to state in the law that it applies retroactively, meaning to past actions too.[[2:19:13]] The committee deferred Bill 99, which would set rules against nepotism (giving jobs to family members).[[2:27:58]] The chair said the bills will come back, but there is no date yet.[[2:31:27]]
decided: A motion to replace Bill 55 with the proposed new (CD1) version was made and seconded; the captions do not clearly show its vote.
meeting.next: Staff will send the Board of Ethics a written question on how often its lobbyist list is updated. The chair will work with staff to bring back the two deferred bills, with no date set yet. The chair said a bill requiring more financial disclosures is in the works.

moments.q: Board chair: three recent cases lost after employees left service
